gm.name: North Macedonia
gm.road_lines: White Outside - White Inside / Yellow Outside - Yellow Inside

items.html:
North Macedonian licence plates are white and sometimes have the standard European blue strip on the left. They also have a noticeable red block near the left side of the licence plate.

NOTE: Serbia will almost always have a blue strip on their licence plates.

All Generation 4 coverage in North Macedonia was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

NOTE: Most of the Balkans and southern Europe have Smallcam.

North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped. They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

NOTE: Croatia uses the same wedge-shaped bollard. Hungary has a similar wedge-shaped bollard but with more white space above the black rectangle.

North Macedonia uses A-Profile guardrails, like most of Europe. The guardrails have red reflectors.

NOTE: Serbia uses B-Profile guardrails. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.

Direction signs in North Macedonia are typically yellow with biscriptal text: town names are written in both Latin and Cyrillic script.

NOTE: Serbia, Slovenia, Croatia, and Montenegro have similar signs. Serbia is the only one that will have biscriptal text though.

Macedonian is a Slavic language which uses the Cyrillic script. Road signs have Latin on them too, although most other signs are fully in Cyrillic.

The letters ‘Ѓ’ and ‘Ќ’ are unique to Macedonian. ‘Љ’, ‘Њ’, and ‘Џ’ are only in Serbian and Macedonian.

There will never be an antenna on the Google car.

Every other country in Europe will have an antenna sometimes in Generation 3 coverage. For clarity’s sake: this means that cars with no antenna can be found outside North Macedonia.

NOTE: The only other country to have no antenna the majority of the time is Serbia, although there will be an antenna sometimes.
The general landscape of North Macedonia consists of relatively dry grasslands, and small hills and scattered trees.
These ‘Greek Lamps’ on utility poles can be found in North Macedonia. They can also be found in various other countries, such as (unsurprisingly) Greece or Serbia.

North Macedonia normally uses yellow-filled in warning signs. Most of Europe uses white ones.

NOTE: In southeastern Europe, Greece also commonly uses yellow-filled in signs. Slovenia sometimes has yellow-filled signs.

Generation 3 Coverage is sparse, only including some highways and some cities in the country.

The cities of Skopje, Bitola, Kumanovo, Prilep, Tetovo, Veles, Ohrid, and Strumica are the only ones with significant coverage inside the city.

You can view the official coverage in more detail on this site.
Skopje is the capital and by far the largest city. If you see any large apartments or buildings, you are almost guaranteed to be in Skopje.

Each city has its own city-specific posters with public obituaries. They are commonly found on utility poles.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
Obituaries in Kumanovo are the most distinct. They are the only obituaries to have a thick light blue border.
Obituaries in Bitola are horizontal and can be either light or dark blue. The cross is in-between the border, leaving a gap in the rectangle.
Obituaries in Ohrid are horizontal and either red or blue. The cross is underneath the border, which is unique to Ohrid when the obituary is red.
Obituaries in Strumica are vertical and blue. They are the only obituaries to have an intricate pattern in the corner of the poster.

Obituaries in Veles are vertical and blue. Veles has the largest variety of obituaries, but will never have the pattern in the corner like the ones seen in Strumica. They are also the only city that will have the cross above the border when blue.
Obituaries in Prilep are vertical and black. The border does not go completely around the poster, which makes it easy to distinguish.
Obituaries in Tetovo are vertical and black. There are 2 main types found in the city, one with the cross above the border and one with a thick cross in-between the border.

If you see black and yellow striped kerbs, you are most likely to be in Strumica.

They are rarely found in Skopje and if you see them around roundabouts, you will most likely be in Tetovo.
Ohrid is the only large city located next to a lake.
These long rectangular lamps are only found in the city of Prilep.
These two extremely rocky hills are visible in some parts of the city of Prilep.

In GENERATION 3 coverage A green truck is visible behind the Google Car for a portion of the E-65. The truck is visible from Kichevo to Arbinovo.

NOTE: This hint is mostly obsolete

lm.name: Bollards
lm.note: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped(looks like Croatia bollard). They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

lm.name: 3 Dots
lm.note: If you see three smudges, you will always be on the R1304. The only large city on this road is Kočani, although it has extremely limited coverage.

lm.name: A road
lm.note:
Road from Tetovo to Ohrid. Some clouds, mountainous, but they are in the distance and not too high. (This applies to both road A and B).

The camera on road A is pretty clean for the most part so if you see any random smudges you probably won't be on this road.

lm.name: B Road
lm.note:
Ohrid to Bitola. Some clouds, mountainous, but they are in the distance and not too high (This applies to both road A and B).

Parts of the road (maybe a majority of it) has a slight smudge that is northwest of the car. I think it is the start of the "one black smudge" coverage but it is much less visable.

lm.name: Bitola obituary
lm.note: These stickers are also horizontally longer in length. They appear to have a black/dark blue border. One important thing to note is cross placement. The cross is in between the border, cutting it off from making a complete rectangle.

lm.name: Black and Yellow Roundabouts
lm.note: Black and Yellow striped curbs in Roundabouts and Intersections can commonly be found in Tetovo. (The can also be seen more rarely in Strumica and Skopje)

lm.name: Black and Yellow St Curbs
lm.note:
Black and yellow curbs that run along the road can commonly be found in Strumica and very rarely Skopje (95% of time its Strumica)

(this does not apply for those on intersections or roundabouts; those can also be black and yellow in Strumica but can be elsewhere

lm.name: Brown Dot
lm.note: If you see a brown smudge, you will be in the far southeast of the country.

lm.name: C Road
lm.note:
Road from Bitola to Prilep. Rather flat, sometimes a small black glitch on the camera. Not too much vegetation.

This road has the "One black smudge" coverage with the smudge northwest of the car. Sometimes there is another one also.

This road also uses these round circular bollards that are visable pretty much everywhere on this road.

lm.name: D Road
lm.note:
Road east from Prilep. Flat in most parts, but much more vegetation (start of the road from Prilep can be a little bit through the mountains, with exposed rock hills in some places that can only be found around Prilep.
Has a bunch of random inconsistant smudges. If you don't see any smudges, its probably not this road.

lm.name: Divided Kumanovo Roads
lm.note:
Im calling all these the divded roads to Kumanovo. There often is much more vegetation between the two lanes.

Part of the A2 and E75 have some smudges.

lm.name: E Road
lm.note:
North road from Skopje to Kumanovo. Rather generic road, road lines often missing or faded.

This road has the East Water Smudge.

lm.name: East Water Smudge
lm.note:
There is a smudge on top of the camera if you look to the front right of the car and then up. It is only on these roads in the east.

Note: Serbia has a similar smudge, but it is to the back right of the car not the front right.

lm.name: F Road
lm.note:
Road from Kumanovo to the Bulgarian border. Very diverse road, sometimes yellow outside lines or brown (rust?) guardrails. In the far eastern part there are men working on the road.

This Road has a round smudge in the front middle upper part of the camera varying in visibility.

This Road has the East Water Smudge

lm.name: Fly Smudge
lm.note: A fly can be seen on the southern portion of the R1205. This is found nowhere else in the country.

lm.name: Green Truck
lm.note: A green truck is visible behind the Google Car for a portion of the E-65. The truck is visible from Kichevo to Arbinovo.

lm.name: H road
lm.note:
Road south from Kumanovo. Pretty dry and flat road. Extremely sunny coverage, basically not a cloud in the sky.

This road can be confused with road I because they are right next to each other w/ similar road angle and look similar. This road drives South, while Road I drives North.

This Road has the East Water Smudge. No other smudges as far as I can tell.

lm.name: I road
lm.note:
Pretty standard road, not too mountainous or lush. Similar to the H road, but that one drives South while this one drives North. The south part of this road has the fly smudge.

This road has the East Water Smudge.

lm.name: J Road
lm.note:
Pretty flat, no glitches. There also is part with all yellow road lines on this road, but definitely not everywhere.

This Road has the East Water Smudge.

lm.name: K Road
lm.note: Standard small road with trees on both sides. In the north you are followed by a beige car.

lm.name: Kumanovo Obituary
lm.note: Obituaries in Kumanovo are the most distinct. They are the only obituaries to have a thick light blue border.

lm.name: L Road
lm.note:
Generally very flat often with ridges on each side off in the distance.

Start of the 3 dots coverage. You can see 3 dots (black dots) on the camera.

This Road has the east water smudge.

lm.name: M Road
lm.note:
Loop: most of this road also had the 3 flies coverage, the eastern part only has one black dot, the northern part none. A bit hilly/mountainous for the most part.

This road has the East Water Smudge

lm.name: N Road
lm.note:
Standard road, east part has rather dark asphalt.

Western Part is through the mountains, eastern part is flat.

The western part of this road has the East Water Smudge

lm.name: North Of Skopje Divided
lm.note:
It also has a small patch of grass between the two guardrails. It might look a little drier in some places.

Has a smudge in the front bottom left.

lm.name: O Road
lm.note:
Big green mountains in the distance.

This Road has the East Water Smudge.

lm.name: Ohrid Obituary
lm.note: Again, these are horizontally longer in length. These stickers can be red or blue. The most important thing to note though, is the thick cross underneath the border. These are exclusive to Ohrid when the sign is horizontally longer, or red. Vertical long variants are very rare.

lm.name: Ohrid St Sign
lm.note: This Street Sign is unique to Ohrid

lm.name: One Black Smudge
lm.note: You can sometimes see some smudges on the camera. If you see one black smudge on the camera, you will most likely be on the A3 between Bitola and Prilep, or the R1302 in the far east. Keep in mind smudges can be randomly seen throughout the country.

lm.name: One Concrete Median
lm.note: The E-65 just south of Tetovo has one concrete median separating each lane instead of a normal guardrail. This is the only highway in the country to have this. It also has these unique red reflectors.

lm.name: One Guardrail Divided Highway
lm.note: Most of the E-75 next to the Greek Border has only one guardrail separating each lane. Some parts have a guardrail on one side and concrete median on the other. These are both only found on this highway.

lm.name: P Road
lm.note:
Brown dot on the camera (you can also find this on the Q road).

This road does not have the distinctive south ridge unlike Q.

The further south you go, it gets more flat and you can even see Dojran lake in some parts.

lm.name: Prilep City Hills
lm.note: These two extremely rocky hills are visible in some parts of the city of Prilep.

lm.name: Prilep Lamps
lm.note: These long rectangular lamps are only found in the city of Prilep.

lm.name: Prilep Obituary v1
lm.note: Prilep is quite distinctive. It is the only city to have an orange/red sticker that is vertically longer. (there is also another version)

lm.name: Prilep Obituary v2
lm.note: Prilip also has another version. It has the double border like in Kumanovo, but it doesn't go all the way around. It stops at the horizontal ends.

lm.name: Skopje South Divided
lm.note:
A bit tricky, just kinda looks like the general Skopje Area.

Parts of the Road have front left lower smudge, parts of the road have all yellow road lines.

lm.name: Skopje Vibe
lm.note: Skopje is the capital and by far the largest city. If you see any large apartments or buildings, you are almost guaranteed to be in Skopje.

lm.name: South of Veles Divided
lm.note: This divided highway has a lot of these short little baby tree things in the median. For a small portion there are normal trees as well.

lm.name: Southeast of Strumica (Q Road)
lm.note:
This large ridge in the south paired with open fields is found on this road east of Strumica. The further east you go on this road, the easier it is to see this ridge.

This road (Q) and the one west of Strumica (P) both have a Brown Smudge.

lm.name: Split Divided
lm.note:
This Road Consists of one road that is split into two directions that are not next to each other. These are the only "one way" roads that are not in a city.

Driving North: This road is under construction and there are a bunch of random things on the road like chevrons, etc., sometimes one of the lanes is blocked off, the pavement often is dark and new, sometimes there are all yellow roadlines, and in the northern part the Yellow truck is following you.

Driving South: There is often cars in both lane driving the same direction and is not under construction, the "center line" is dashed (this is not unique but uncommon elsewhere). It is quite hilly and there is a river following the road on the west side (which you can't see but you can tell it is there because there is a ravine). Northern part of the road has a front left bottom smudge.

lm.name: Strumica Obituary
lm.note: Obituaries in Strumica are vertical and blue. They are the only obituaries to have an intricate pattern in the corner of the poster.

lm.name: Tetevo to Skopje Divided
lm.note:
The middle of this road has a small patch of grass between two guardrails. The further east on this road, the more trees between the two lanes.

The only other road you get trees between the lanes is a small section of the road south of Veles.

lm.name: Tetovo Obituary
lm.note: Obituaries in Tetovo are vertical and black. There are 2 main types found in the city, one with the cross above the border and one with a thick cross in-between the border.

lm.name: Veles Obituary
lm.note: Obituaries in Veles are vertical and blue. Veles has the largest variety of obituaries, but will never have the pattern in the corner like the ones seen in Strumica. They are also the only city that will have the cross above the border when blue.

lm.name: Yellow Lines
lm.note:
For some of the E-75 north of Veles, there are triple yellow lines with a dashed centre line. In the northern part of the road, there is a yellow-truck following the Google car.

A section of the A3 east of Veles also has triple yellow lines, which in Europe is extremely uncommon.

lm.name: Yellow Truck
lm.note:
In the northern part of the E-75 north of Veles, there is a yellow-truck following the Google car.

(The rest of the road is either under construction or newly paved. This road is very similar to the A3 east of Veles, although that one is much flatter and has an arid landscape surrounding it)

lm.name: Smudges
lm.note: In southern and eastern North Macedonia, some roads have recognizable smudges on the camera: A large dead insect on the R1205, a vertical pattern of about four smudges on the PS27, a central smudge (plus more further south) on the easternmost part of the A3, a brown smudge on the lower left center in the southeast of the country, and on the A1 to Bitola, a single smudge higher up to the left with a short section of two brown smudges center left halfway between Bitola and Prilep

lm.name: Macedonian
lm.note:
Macedonian is a South Slavic language closely related to Bulgarian. Macedonian uses the Cyrillic script. Road signs have Latin on them too, although most other signs are fully in Cyrillic.

The letters Ѓ and Ќ are unique to Macedonian. Љ, Њ, and Џ are only used in Serbo-Croatian and Macedonian (not in Bulgarian). The same goes for the letter J (loaned from Latin), where Й is used in Bulgarian instead. Bulgarian uses the letter Ъ which is not found in Macedonian or Serbo-Croatian.

The Macedonian word for street is улица (ulitsa), like most Slavic languages.

lm.name: Skopje mountains
lm.note: Skopje has mountains in the north and south, the north mountain is even bigger and you can often see a cross on top of it.
